original_question: A group G is said to be virtually special if G has a finite-index subgroup isomorphic to the fundamental group of a special complex(in the sense of F. Haglund, D. T. Wise, Geom. Funct. Anal., 17, no. 5(2008), 1551–1620; cf 20.60.) A group G is called a CAT(0) group if it acts properly discontinuously and cocompactly by isometries on a CAT(0) metric space. a) Is every CAT(0) free-by-cyclic group virtually special? b) A weaker question: does every CAT(0) free-by-cyclic group virtually embed into a right-angled Artin group?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.124(a)-(b) in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": whether every CAT(0) free-by-cyclic group is virtually special, and, more weakly, whether every such group virtually embeds into a right-angled Artin group. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the official formulation: it reproduces the paper's definitions of "virtually special" and "CAT(0) group" and keeps both parts of the problem, including the weaker right-angled-Artin-group embedding question. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, define "free-by-cyclic" explicitly as a group G with a normal free subgroup F such that G/F is cyclic; elsewhere in the notebook, the split infinite-cyclic case is written as G = F_n ⋊ Z. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Clarify that "special complex" means a Haglund-Wise special cube complex, which is the notion referenced in Problem 21.124 and cross-referred to via Problem 20.60. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
Clarify that "virtually embed into a right-angled Artin group" means that some finite-index subgroup of G embeds into a right-angled Artin group. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Let G be a CAT(0) free-by-cyclic group, meaning that G has a normal free subgroup F with cyclic quotient G/F and that G acts properly discontinuously and cocompactly by isometries on a CAT(0) metric space. Must G be virtually special, i.e. must some finite-index subgroup of G be isomorphic to the fundamental group of a Haglund-Wise special cube complex? More weakly, must some finite-index subgroup of G embed into a right-angled Artin group?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem 21.124, so the correct target is that exact two-part problem, not the narrower neighboring Problem 21.125 about polynomially growing automorphisms. The only real omissions are standard terms left implicit by the notebook: what "free-by-cyclic" means and what "virtually embed" means. The cross-reference to Problem 20.60 identifies the intended Haglund-Wise notion of specialness, but 21.124 itself asks about "virtually special" and does not add extra hypotheses such as compactness, growth conditions, or a specific presentation. Part (b) is explicitly presented only as a weaker question, so no equivalent reformulation should be substituted. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
